newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Heiton turnover ahead in 4 months to end-Aug.
newsitem.headline: Heiton turnover ahead in 4 months to end-Aug.

text.p: Irish builders merchants Heiton Holdings Plc said on Thursday that turnover in the four months to end-August was ahead of last year.

"The outlook remains positive and I am confident that in the absence of unforseen circumstances, progress will be maintained in the current year," Chairman Stephen O'Connor told the centenary annual meeting.
The company said that on a like-for-like basis, higher sales were recorded in its homecare division although this was offset by the loss of a Dublin store in a fire in June.

Heiton said arrangements had been made to maintain its market presence in the area by opening a small, adjoining store on July 27 pending the rebuilding of the main premises which should be up and running by early summer next year.
The group said its builders merchants and steel division continued to progress well.
"The buoyancy in the construction industry is being sustained with continued growth in all sectors -- private residential, commercial and the public sector."
Heiton said it expected this buoyancy to be maintained through 1996 although the rate and pace of growth, especially in the residential sector, may slow down a bit into 1997.
O'Connor said growth in the hotel and leisure sector had been exceptionally strong and would continue to be a major source of business for Heitons in the current year.
The company said steel prices now appeared to have bottomed out and it was seeing improving demand in Europe which augured well for its steel stockholding business.
Heiton reported a 72 percent increase in pre-tax profits to 6.9 million punts in the year to April 30, 1996 while turnover rose by nine percent.
